THEIR CERTIFICATES OF               §

FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST            §
SWITCH TO BIG HILL                  §
SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE §
IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL,   §
LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,             §
MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, §
SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,    §
AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES             §

    INTERVENOR DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL POST-HEARING BRIEF

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

        Dance Bar Ranch, LLC (“DBR”) submits this Initial Post-Hearing Brief in PUC Dkt. No.

59475 and respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges recommend denial of the Joint

Application (the “Application”) of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA

Transmission Services Corporation (the “Applicants”) in its entirety. Alternatively, if the project

is approved, the decision should reject any route that includes Link V1.

                   I.      INTRODUCTION AND STATEMENT OF POSITION

        1.      This case involves an unprecedented 765-kV transmission proposal with

extraordinary and permanent consequences for landowners, communities, and critical local

infrastructure. The record does not demonstrate compliance with the Public Utility Regulatory

Act’s routing and public-interest requirements. In alignment with the concerns and themes

advanced in a brief 1 filed by American Stewards of Liberty in a companion 765-kV proceeding,



1
 See American Stewards of Liberty's Initial Closing Argument, PUC Docket No. 59315, Item No. 5555 (filed May
18, 2026).

DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL BRIEF                                                                      1
 the Commission should deny this Application.

       2.      In alignment with the broader public interest, the Commission should deny this

Application. At a minimum—and of vital consequence to DBR—the Commission must reject any

route utilizing Link V1. The record establishes that Link V1 is a fatally flawed routing option for

three independent reasons:

            a. Fails Prudent Avoidance: Routes utilizing Link V1 average 125 or more habitable

               structures, substantially exceeding the Applicants’ preferred route (Route 894),

               which impacts only 85 habitable structures.

            b. Threatens Protected Wildlife: The Applicants’ Environmental Assessment

               erroneously asserts that the project will have zero impact on bald eagles. Direct

               testimony and evidence from DBR, along with evidence from other landowners,

               soundly refute this claim, establishing active bald eagle hunting and roosting

               habitats along various corridors of the project, including Link V1.

            c. Presents Severe Engineering and Construction Risks: Geological and structural

               constraints, specifically the presence of unstable alluvial sands along the San Saba

               River corridor, create severe long-term risks to the construction and physical

               integrity of the massive 765-kV transmission towers on Link V1.

                               II.     FACTUAL BACKGROUND

       3.      Intervenor Dance Bar Ranch, LLC is an active, historic working ranch located at

1217 CR 340, Richland Springs, Texas. See Dance Bar Ranch – 1. The ranch was originally

purchased in 1859 by Headley Lamar Polk, a kinsman of U.S. President James K. Polk, and the

ranch is formally recognized by the Texas Historical Commission (Historical Marker Atlas No.

5411002806). See id. The property encompasses critical agricultural resources, livestock



DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL BRIEF                                                             2
 operations, and unique environmental habitats along three and one-half miles of the San Saba River

frontage. See id.

       4.      Proposed Link V1 directly intersects the Dance Bar Ranch, slicing through its

northern, high-fenced pastures along Hwy 190 and extending to the San Saba River. See id.; see

Dance Bar Ranch – 6. If selected, Link V1 would impose a massive 765-kV transmission easement

with structures reaching heights of nearly 200 feet. See Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1, p. 7, 9.

       5.      Link V1 is utilized in Routes 392, 402, 410, and 416. See Oncor & LCRA TSC –

1, p. 2780-2781.

                                         III.    ARGUMENT

   A. The Application Should Be Denied Because the Record Fails to Demonstrate Compliance

       with PURA § 37.056

       6.      PURA requires an evidence-based showing that the project is needed and that

routing reasonably balances community values, environmental integrity, historical/aesthetic

values, and prudent avoidance. PURA § 37.056. The Commission’s approval of the Permian Basin

Reliability Plan does not relieve Applicants of their burden to demonstrate that the requested CCN

amendment satisfies PURA § 37.056.

       7.      The scale of the Project is unprecedented. Applicants estimate transmission-line

costs ranging from approximately $1.64 billion to $1.86 billion, excluding an additional $395

million in station costs at Bell County East Switch. See Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1, p. 7. The public

notice filed in this docket states that total project costs may range from approximately $2.03 billion

to $2.25 billion, depending upon the route selected by the Commission. See id., pp. 1850-1870.

       8.      Although Applicants rely on the Permian Basin Reliability Plan as support for the

Project, ERCOT's underlying analysis reflects a policy choice among multiple transmission-



DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL BRIEF                                                                3
 development alternatives. See id., pp. 19-26. ERCOT evaluated traditional 345-kV facilities as

well as 500-kV and 765-kV extra-high-voltage options and acknowledged that each option satisfies

reliability criteria. See id., p. 24-25. ERCOT further noted that additional systemwide evaluation

of extra-high-voltage facilities was ongoing when the Permian Basin Reliability Plan was

presented to the Commission. See id. This record evidence undermines any claim that the

Applicants have established the necessity of this specific proposal.

       9.      Accordingly, the Commission must independently evaluate whether the proposed

facilities and route satisfy PURA § 37.056. That obligation is particularly important here because

the project would introduce some of the first 765-kV transmission facilities in Texas, with

structures reaching approximately 198 feet in height and crossing a study area extending roughly

200 miles across Central Texas. See id., pp. 7, 9.

       10.     The Environmental Assessment also acknowledges that no formal cultural-resource

survey has yet been conducted on the alternative routes, and that unknown archaeological and

historic resources may be encountered along the ultimately approved route. See Oncor & LCRA

TSC – 1, p. 253. It likewise recognizes that route-specific impacts cannot be fully evaluated until

a final route is selected. See id., pp. 235, 237; TR. Vol. 2 at 174-175. These admissions confirm

that the Applicants have not provided the complete, route-specific analysis required by PURA.

       11.     Because the Applicants have failed to present sufficient, reliable, and complete

evidence to satisfy PURA § 37.056(c)—including with respect to need for service, community

values, environmental integrity, and historical and aesthetic impacts—the Commission cannot

lawfully approve the Application. The Application should therefore be denied.




DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL BRIEF                                                             4
      IV.     Alternatively, If the Project Is Approved, Any Route Utilizing Link V1 Should
                                                Be Rejected

   A. Link V1 Unnecessarily Increases Impacts to Nearby Homes

       12.     Link V1 performs worse than the Applicants’ preferred route with respect to

proximity to habitable structures—a clear, objective routing factor. PURA § 37.056; 16 Tex.

Admin. Code § 25.101. The Applicants’ preferred route has approximately 85 habitable structures

within 500 feet of the centerline, whereas all routes that include Link V1 average approximately

125 homes within that distance. See Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1, p. 1992-2053.

       13.     This substantial increase in nearby homes is a straightforward and compelling

reason to avoid Link V1. While no single routing factor is dispositive, habitable‑structure

proximity is one of the most visible and easily understood measures of community impact. The

record shows that selecting routes, like the Applicants’ preferred route, without Link V1 materially

reduces these impacts.

   B. The Environmental Assessment is Factually Flawed Regarding Bald Eagle Habitats

       14.     The Environmental Assessment and Routing Study prepared for the Applicants by

Kimley-Horn and Halff expressly states in Section 3.5.2.4 that:

       “No bald eagles, bald eagle nests, or habitat for bald eagles were observed within the study

       area; therefore, the proposed project is not anticipated to impact this species.”

Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1, p. 170.

However, the evidentiary record demonstrates that this critical desktop finding is incorrect. See

Dance Bar Ranch – 1. The direct testimony of Myles Dance confirms that bald eagles actively

roost, hunt, and forage along the San Saba River corridor within the proposed Link V1 footprint.

See id. DBR has corroborated this testimony with geolocation data and other evidence

documenting bald eagle activity on the ranch. See id. In addition, other parties submitted testimony

DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL BRIEF                                                              5
 and evidence regarding bald eagle nests within the study area and the project’s potential impacts

on those resources. TR. Vol. 3 at 154–55.

        15.     The bald eagle is strictly protected under the federal Bald and Golden Eagle

Protection Act and the Migratory Bird Treaty Act. Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act, 16

U.S.C. §§ 668-668d (2024). Slicing through this active riparian hunting canopy with a 765-kV line

creates severe electrocution and habitat fragmentation risks that the Environmental Assessment

utterly failed to evaluate.

    C. Unstable Alluvial Sands Present Severe Construction and Engineering Constraints

        16.     Beyond the environmental and community impacts associated with Link V1, the

record demonstrates that the route traverses portions of the San Saba River floodplain

characterized by alluvial deposits and river-bottom soils. See Dance Bar Ranch – 1. The

construction of approximately 198-foot-tall 765-kV transmission structures requires substantial

foundation support and site-specific engineering. See Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1, p. 67. Applicants

acknowledged that geologic conditions can affect foundation design and that areas presenting

subsurface challenges may require specialized engineering and construction techniques. TR. Vol.

2 at 269-270, 276. Applicants further testified that when structures are located in geologically

sensitive areas, specialized construction practices and additional geotechnical evaluation may be

necessary. See id., p. 271.

        17.     Unlike stable upland terrain, river-bottom alluvial deposits are subject to flooding,

erosion, sediment movement, and variable subsurface conditions. As a result, the presence of

extensive alluvial soils along Link V1 creates additional engineering uncertainty and foundation-

design challenges that are not present, or are substantially reduced, on available upland

alternatives. Applicants admitted that construction in karst terrain may require specialized



DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL BRIEF                                                               6
 construction practices and increase costs. See id., p. 275-276. The Commission should therefore

consider whether routing a 765-kV facility through floodplain alluvial deposits is prudent where

alternative routes avoid or minimize those geotechnical constraints.

   D. PUC Staff’s Recommendation Is Entitled to Limited Weight Given the Novelty of 765-kV
      Facilities

       18.     The Commission should independently evaluate Staff’s routing recommendation in

light of the limited number of 765-kV transmission projects that have been reviewed in Texas. TR.

Vol. 4 at 85-87. The record reflects that Staff witness John Poole has reviewed only one other 765-

kV transmission-line proceeding. See id. As a result, Staff’s recommendation is not grounded in

extensive experience with extra-high-voltage transmission routing across diverse projects,

applicants, or geographic regions. This limitation is particularly significant because the project

would involve some of the first 765-kV facilities in Texas and presents routing, land-use,

environmental, and community-impact considerations that differ substantially from traditional

transmission projects. See Oncor & LCRA TSC – 1, pp. 7, 9. Accordingly, the Commission should

place greater emphasis on the objective routing evidence in the record—including habitable-

structure impacts and effects on water-district planning—than on generalized routing

recommendations. Those objective metrics demonstrate that routes utilizing Link V1 create greater

impacts than available alternatives.

   E. The Applicants’ Own Expert Witness Recommends a Route Excluding Link V1

       19.     Notably, the Applicants’ own expert engineering and routing witness, Casey D.

Petty, P.E., identified “Route 894 as the route that best meets the requirements of the Texas Utilities

Code and the Commission’s Substantive Rules” for this project. Oncor & LCRA TSC – 5, p. 10.

In direct testimony and an accompanying routing memorandum, Ms. Petty concluded that Route

894 is the option that best balances engineering constraints, costs, environmental factors, and the

DANCE BAR RANCH, LLC’S INITIAL BRIEF                                                                 7
 Commission's substantive routing rules under PURA. See id., p. 12. Because Route 894 does not

utilize Link V1, there is no rational, record-based justification to select a highly damaging

alternative route that incorporates Link V1.

                        CONCLUSION AND PRAYER FOR RELIEF

       For the foregoing reasons, Dance Bar Ranch, LLC respectfully requests that the

Administrative Law Judges:

   (a) Recommend denial of the Joint Application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and

       LCRA Transmission Services Corporation; and

   (b) In the alternative, if the project is approved, recommend rejection of any route using Link

       V1; and

   (c) Grant such other and further relief to which Dance Bar Ranch, LLC may be justly entitled.

Date: June 18, 2026

                                                           Respectfully submitted,
